The set \(\{1011,1012,\dots,2020\}\) has \(2020-1011+1=1010\) numbers, and no element divides another since any multiple of a number \(>1010\) exceeds \(2020\).

For the upper bound, write every integer as \(q\cdot 2^k\), where \(q\) is odd. Numbers with the same odd part form a divisibility chain, so at most one can be chosen from each chain. There are \(1010\) odd numbers in \(\{1,\dots,2020\}\), so at most \(1010\) numbers can be chosen.

Thus the maximum is \(\boxed{1010}\).
